definition: A lasting advantage that protects a business the way water protects a castle.
example: The difference between GEICO's costs and those of its competitors is a kind of moat that protects a valuable business castle.

definition: The range of businesses you can evaluate honestly, and whose edge you can see.
example: You only have to be able to evaluate companies within your circle of competence.

definition: The edge of what you understand. Knowing it matters more than widening it.
example: The size of that circle is not very important; knowing the boundary, however, is vital.

definition: Belonging to the business itself, as distinct from the price the market is quoting.
example: When companies with good economics sell well below intrinsic business value, stocks sometimes provide grand-slam home runs.

definition: The trust a firm has earned, which he says cannot be traded away for a profit.
example: We can afford to lose money, but we can't afford to lose reputation — even a shred of reputation.

definition: Only average, and therefore hurt rather than helped by the passing of time.
example: Time is the friend of the wonderful business, the enemy of the mediocre.

definition: A business position so strong that customers and economics stay with it.
example: Widening the moat by driving down costs defends and strengthens the economic franchise.

definition: A departure from the usual, here a market price swung by fear or greed.
example: The market aberrations produced by fear and greed are unpredictable, both as to duration and degree.

definition: A rush of confidence that lifts prices free of the businesses underneath them.
example: Little fear is visible in Wall Street. Instead, euphoria prevails.

definition: Honesty and soundness of character, the trait he wants in the managers he keeps.
example: They love their businesses, they think like owners, and they exude integrity and ability.

definition: With a grip that will not let go, even when the thing held is disappointing.
example: We are the opposite of those who tenaciously hang on to businesses that disappoint.

definition: Sensible in light of the value, not merely exciting.
example: Your goal should be to purchase, at a rational price, a part interest in an easily understandable business.

definition: The underlying way a business makes or fails to make money.
example: When a brilliant management tackles a business with a reputation for bad economics, it is the reputation of the business that remains intact.

definition: Exceptional cleverness, which he says still loses to a bad business.
example: A management with a reputation for brilliance cannot outrun a business with bad economics.

definition: Without mercy. The stance he takes toward a loss of reputation, not toward a loss of money.
example: Lose a shred of reputation for the firm, and I will be ruthless.

definition: Willing to wait. In his image, the party who receives money from the restless.
example: The stock market serves as a relocation center at which money is moved from the active to the patient.

definition: Grasping for more when prices and moods are already high.
example: We simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.

definition: To put a large stake into a few things you understand, rather than a little into many.
example: We continue to concentrate our investments in a very few companies that we try to understand well.

definition: Worn away. A bargain's early edge disappears when the business earns little.
example: Any initial advantage you secure will be quickly eroded by the low return that the business earns.

definition: Spreading quickly from person to person, as he says fear and greed do.
example: Occasional outbreaks of those two super-contagious diseases, fear and greed, will forever occur in the investment community.

definition: Clearly above the ordinary, the sort of business he wants to hold without a sale date.
example: When we own portions of outstanding businesses with outstanding managements, our favorite holding period is forever.

definition: Clear enough that you can explain how the business will earn money years from now.
example: Purchase a part interest in an easily-understandable business whose earnings are virtually certain to be higher years from now.
